slides.title: Reversing Harlow's margin decline

paragraphs.text: Reversing Harlow's margin decline
Margin plan for the board meeting, February 2027
Harlow Fresh Markets
Board of directors, presented by the CEO
Board confidential; fictional company, synthetic briefing data

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Fix promotions, shrink and home delivery rather than cut labor: margin reaches about 2.3% by FY2028, and 3.0% only if nearly everything goes right
Wages are not the main cause: gross margin and e-commerce fulfillment explain 79% of the margin decline
–	Store labor explains only 13% of the fall from 3.37% to 1.02% margin
Promotions and e-commerce are not earning what their teams told the board
–	38% of FY2025 promotions lost money; e-commerce lost about $10M, mostly on delivery
Management's 8% labor cut would net about $8M, not $14.5M, because shrink rises where hours are thin
–	The leanest-staffed stores lose 3.1% of sales to shrink, against 2.3% in the best-staffed
Five moves worth about $25M a year lift margin to about 2.3% by FY2028 after the wage rise, short of 3.0%
–	Cutting promotions is worth $10.5M a year; six store exits add $4.4M
–	The labor-cut draft would leave margin near 1.3%
Delivery fees, promotion cuts and shrink fixes go first; the CFO should open covenant talks with the lender now
–	If the decline stops, wave 1 needs 29% of its value to clear the $20M covenant

The gross-margin fall comes entirely from deeper promotions and higher shrink, both within Harlow's control
Gross margin, % of sales, FY2023 to FY2025, change by driver
of gross profit a year lost to the two drifts, at FY2025 sales
▪	Promotional mix: promotions rose from 24% to 29% of sales, each sale earning 14 percentage points less margin
▪	Vendor funding: vendors now cover 46% of markdowns, down from 55%, so each event costs Harlow more
▪	Shrink: up from 2.1% to 2.6% of sales as hours per sale fell
▪	Private label: share rose from 17.0% to 18.5% at 12 percentage points more margin, too slowly to offset
1  Mix effects use the margin gaps in the briefing pack (promotions −14 pp, private label +12 pp, both unchanged); the three drivers explain the full change

The net figure is likely an upper bound
▪	Shrink rose 0.5 percentage points as hours per $1,000 of sales fell 6% in FY2023–25; only its staff-sensitive 65% is assumed to respond to a further 8% cut
▪	If theft responds to thinner staffing too, the net saving falls to about $4.5M a year
▪	Lost sales from longer checkout waits and stock-outs are not counted, while ValuMart keeps opening nearby
▪	The 2027 minimum-wage rise of 4% adds about $7.3M a year to the labor bill under either plan
The draft also freezes e-commerce at a loss and leaves promotions and shrink untouched
